newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close weaker in thin turnover.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close weaker in thin turnover.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks largely ignored higher interest rates and strong property prices to limp to a slightly weaker close on Wednesday, brokers said.
"If good pre-sales and good land auctions won't drive the market, then we're running into a situation whereby what will?" said James Osborne, sales director with ING Barings.
Brokers said higher U.S. interest rates had been factored into share prices and investors could be looking to Wall Street for a lead before the Easter holiday from Friday to Monday.
The Hang Seng Index closed at 12,776.39, down 56.14 points or 0.44 percent.
Turnover was HK$7.27 billion, down from Tuesday's HK$10.33 billion.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the territory's de facto central bank, raised a key interest rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday morning, and the Hong Kong Association of Banks raised deposit rates by the same amount.
The increases followed Tuesday's 25 basis point rise in the U.S federal funds rate to 5-1/2 percent.
Richard Verin, head of equities trading at CS First Boston, said the market might take a lead from Wall Street, adding that people were reluctant to take a position ahead of a long weekend.
Sino Land, which on Tuesday paid a record HK$11.82 billion for a site at a government land auction, slipped to HK$8.15, down HK$0.30 or 3.55 percent.
Brokers said fears that Sino Land might make a cash call to help raise funds to develop the site fuelled the selling.
Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$0.75 to HK$85.25, and Wharf slipped HK$0.70 to HK$31.20.

Brokers said the closure of the March Hang Seng Index futures contract was largely uneventful, but added that the April index futures contract was trading at a discount to the cash index, suggesting short-term bearishness.
Citic Pacific, which reported net profits for 1996 of HK$6.86 billion, largely in line with market expectations, closed at HK$38.50, down HK$0.30.
Cheung Kong gained HK$0.50 to close at HK$70.50 and Hutchison Whampoa rose HK$0.25 to HK$58.00.
On Wednesday, Cheung Kong reported net earnings for 1996 of $13.77 billion, up from HK$11.13 billion in 1995, and Hutchison posted 1996 net profit of HK$12.02 billion, up from HK$9.57 billion.
